summary: Standing R-6 tower six miles from Missoula; site developed 1934, present tower built 1957 at Davis Point and moved here in 1966.

events.note: Site developed with a 40-ft pole tower and L-4 cab
Red Skies of Montana filmed on location; the register ties the tower to the film, which conflicts with the 1957 build date
Present 41-ft tower built at Davis Point
Moved from Davis Point to Blue Mountain to replace an older timber tower
Lolo Creek Complex fire, still several miles from the tower's northern edge; tower being fire-wrapped and sprinklers put in as a precaution
Closed for the summer for repairs

corrections.why: The register and firelookout.com both describe the present tower as 41 feet. 12.2 m is 40 feet, the height of the 1934 pole tower.

corrections.proposed: 1934 built (40-ft pole tower); 1957 built at Davis Point (present 41-ft tower); 1966 relocated to Blue Mountain
corrections.why: The tower standing today was built in 1957 at another site and moved in 1966. The 1934 entry describes only the first tower.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Not resolved. The register says the tower was used in filming Red Skies of Montana while on Davis Point. KGVO dates the filming to 1952. KGVO and firelookout.com date the tower's build to 1957. The sources do not explain how these fit together, so the story says so.

sources.title: Update – Firefighters Protect Historic Blue Mountain Fire Lookout

notes_for_editor: Access level omitted: the register gives no access rule, and the 2013 KGVO report is the only road description. No staffing key: the register calls it active, undated. Elevation not used: the register gives 1,940 m, and a search summary gave a different figure I could not confirm on a fetched page. A search summary mentioned a 37-year lookout staffer; it was not on any fetched page, so it is left out. Film-date conflict is unresolved and flagged in the story.
